{{Infobox place|name=The Banner-lands|type=Continent|image=Fanlanden map.jpg|caption=Plate I — the Banner-lands, general chart, 396 A.U.|notable=The known world; named for the [[War of the Unification|War of the Eleven Banners]]|sources=[[Chronicle of Victory]]; [[Plate I]]; the Atlas of the Banner-lands}}
'''The Banner-lands''' are the known world of [[Emberwold (series)|Emberwold]]: a single, kidney-shaped continent, bounded by [[the Sleeping Sea]] in the west and south and by [[the Silent Mountains]] in the east and north, where the map — and the certainty — ends.

The continent takes its name from the war that made it one realm: the people remember ''eleven banners'' on the field, though the official record counts ten.<ref>The name is itself a miscount that survived; see [[War of the Unification]].</ref>

== The shape of the land ==
* '''[[The Ash Fields]]''' — the fertile, densely populated heartland, where the decisive battle was fought and the [[Ash Oath]] sworn. At its center lies [[The seat of power|the seat of power]], which bears three conflicting names.
* '''[[The Sleeping Sea]]''' (west/south) — navigable near the coast, fog-bound farther out. Few ships return from the deep sea; those that do carry contradictory stories.
* '''[[The Silent Mountains]]''' (east/north) — one enormous system that walls the known world, bending along the northern rim into the far northwest. Beyond it: rumors of "the houseless."
* '''[[The Shards]]''' (south) — a scattered island chain with its own maritime culture, half-independent, seat of [[House Tidebreaker]].

The rivers of the Banner-lands are deliberately unnamed on every chart — the Wave-Reader rule: ''"draw the water, omit the quarrel."''

== The ten houses in the periphery ==
Nature shaped each house's philosophy: the fog-coast taught [[House Ravenshade|Ravenshade]] to know first; the boundless grass of [[the Expanses]] taught [[House Stormrider|Stormrider]] that division was death; the high silent valleys taught [[House Whitehart|Whitehart]] to listen. Only the center belongs to no one.
